newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers mainly steady, quiet.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers mainly steady, quiet.

text.p: Middle East very large crude carrier (VLCC) rates were steady in quiet Monday trade, brokers said.
Mideast/Japan rates were steady at W65 for a modern ship, with voyages to Singapore at W60 and to the west at W55.
"There's a quiet but steady tone to the market and I see no reason for rates to fall this week," one VLCC broker said.
The 260,000 tonne, 1995-built Ellen Maersk was said fixed at W61.5 Mideast/Onsan for Ssangyong, while the 262,000 tonne Star Japan was done at W60 Mideast/Singapore for Exxon.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf voyages were also steady.
The 260,000 tonne Stena Concept was done at W65 for Morgan Stanley, while North Sea/USAC VLCCs were likewise assessed at about this level.

In the Med, one VLCC was heard done, the 300,000 tonne Settebello at W80 Sidi Kreir/Fos at W80 for Exxon, while Suezmaxes (130,000 tonners) and Aframaxes (80,000 tonners) were steady in quiet trade at W95 and W102.5 respectively.

The inter-U.K./Cont 80,000 tonne market was lacklustre at W90/95 but 25,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes firmed to W195 from W185 in anticipation of the Baltic export season as well as a lack of tonnage, brokers said.
But 25,000 tonne cross-Med fuel oil dipped to W175/180 from W190 as product was moved onto bigger ships and with a long tonnage list which would take time to be absorbed, they added.
In the Western Hemisphere, 70,000 tonne crude and 50,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes both edged up to W172.5 and W215 respectively.
One broker said there had been "a bit of an empty-out on crude at the end of last week which has caused a shortage of early ships, but I'm not sure if things are going to continue moving up."
